title: Probe Coalescer and Graceful Shedder for Regional SLO Preservation
creator: Avery Sinclair
description:
Background: We continue to see autoscaler oscillation and cascading regional failovers when probe storms coincide with transient GC/IO spikes. Existing probe fanout amplifies noise across replicas and regions, causing the autoscaler to under- or over-react and violating SLOs during bursty traffic. Goal: Implement a Probe Coalescer (server-side aggregation + jittered sampling) and a Graceful Shedder (tokenized admission + progressive degradation) to stabilize autoscaling and preserve customer-facing SLOs during regional perturbations.

What we're building:
- Probe Coalescer: a lightweight local aggregator at the node-level that coalesces liveness/readiness pings for services on the same host and exposes an aggregate health vector to the control plane. The coalescer will support configurable windows (50-500ms), percentile-based thresholds, and per-service weighting.
- Jittered Sampling: adaptive sampling rates by request shape (inference length, token-cost) so heavy requests are sampled at lower frequency for probes while maintaining representativeness for autoscaler signals.
- Probe Hysteresis Engine: configurable hysteresis and staged state transitions (healthy -> degraded-soft -> degraded-hard -> draining) with exponential backoff to avoid flip-flopping during flapping conditions.
- Tokenized Graceful Shedder: admission layer that applies token budgets per-customer and per-region. Tokens allow priority traffic to bypass shedding; non-priority requests are gently deferred with a fallback model or short-circuit response where applicable. The shedder integrates with the admission controller to signal autoscaler-relevant metrics (shed_rate, token_consumption).
- Circuit Fallback Policy: when a region reaches a critical degraded state, requests are routed via smart failover rules to secondary regions or downgraded model variants with a documented latency/cost trade-off matrix.

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
- During synthetic probe-storm tests (see test harness), p95 tail latency for control-plane-aware routes stays within 1.2x baseline and availability SLO remains >= 99.95% for customer-tokens marked high-priority.
- Autoscaler oscillation count (scale-up/scale-down within 10m) is reduced by >= 60% in replayed production windows.
- Synthetic chaos run: regional failure + probe storm shows failover completes within target 30s for critical traffic and soft-degraded traffic recovers within 120s.
- Telemetry: new metrics emitted and visible in runtime-dashboard: probe_coalescer_rate, probe_coalescer_window_ms, probe_hysteresis_state, shed_rate_by_token, token_backpressure_events.

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- Coalescing reduces signal fidelity for per-container micro-fluctuations but improves signal-to-noise for autoscalers. We bias towards preserving SLOs for user-facing traffic at the expense of per-instance immediate corrective action.
- Tokenized shedding increases complexity (billing/partitioning concerns) but gives fine-grained control to protect high-value customers during systemic stress.
- Fallback to downgraded model variants trades quality for latency/cost; this must be surfaced in docs and opt-in per project.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Prototype Probe Coalescer library (libprobe-coalesce) with in-process and sidecar modes. Unit tests + microbenchmarks. (Week 1)
2) Implement hysteresis engine and state machine; integrate with health signaling pipeline and autoscaler feed. (Week 2)
3) Build tokenized shedder API + admission-controller hook; add flags to enable per-customer token allocation. (Week 3)
4) End-to-end tests with replayed production traces; chaos experiments (region isolate + probe storms). (Week 4)
5) Gradual rollout: internal beta -> customer canary -> region-wide rollout with throttled enablement. (Week 5)

Testing and validation:
- Replay harness: extend ENG-68211 synthetic warmup probe harness to feed realistic tokenized traffic patterns and probe bursts. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Probe+Replay+Harness (internal).
- PR for coalescer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/11208 (draft).
- Dashboard: temporary dashboard at https://dash.redwood.ai/d/runtime/probe-coalesce-experiments.

Observability and alarms:
- New SLO alert rules: when shed_rate_by_token > 0.5% AND autoscaler_oscillation > 3 in 10m -> page on-call SRE (P0).
- Create burn-rate dashboard for canary customers to ensure token policies don't inadvertently throttle them.

Docs and runbook:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=64200123 (design + choice matrix).
- Runbook excerpt included in PR description that details rollback steps: disable coalescer flag -> revert token allocations -> promote fallback routing.

Rollout plan and phasing:
- Phase A (internal): enable coalescer in two staging regions with token budget set to 100% passthrough for all customers. Run replayed storms to validate metric stability.
- Phase B (customer canary): enable tokenized shedding for 3 non-critical customers with explicit opt-in and daily telemetry review.
- Phase C (soft-region deploy): enable fallback policies in one production region with gradual token quotas by customer tier.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Coalescing hides failing containers causing slow detection of resource exhaustion. Mitigation: coalescer exposes per-container fallback health and sets thresholds to escalate if a container reports persistent hard errors.
- Risk: Token policies misconfigured and throttling critical customers. Mitigation: conservative defaults, canary groups, and automated rollback on burn-rate anomalies.

Next steps:
- Merge prototype PR and run microbenchmarks (#11208).
- Schedule chaos run with SRE and Oncall to validate failover timing (owner: Diego Marquez).
- Coordinate PM and Solutions to draft customer-facing docs for service degradation behavior.
